Purpose: To deliver events to a destination other than the primary event file.
Caller and time: The one event writer, after it has written an event to the primary file.
Inputs: `open`: the context of the run. `write`: one event, in the order of `seq`. `flush`, `close` and
`status`: nothing. A sink declares the range of event schema majors it accepts.
The context of `open` holds: the identifiers of the run (`runId`, `launchId`, `engineStartId`,
feature, workspace); the four as-is labels `job`, `service.name`, `task` and `backend`, which the
as-is form of a payload needs; the profile and the resolved switches that concern sinks; a
content accessor, which returns content by reference, redacted, and returns nothing while
capture is off; and read access to the table of the compatibility projection, from which a sink
learns the as-is name of an event. The content accessor serves the compatibility projection with
its own as-is snippets whatever the switch of content capture says.
Outputs: None that the run depends on. `status` returns the delivery status of the sink as one line and
as a record: sink label, receiver state, the last delivery status and its reason.
Errors: Every error is contained in the sink. The writer records `telemetry.delivery` and goes on.
Guarantees of the core: Local first: the primary file is written before any sink is called, and it is authoritative. The
primary file writer is part of the core and is not replaceable. Events reach a sink already
redacted. The event file holds references to content and never content; content reaches a sink
only through the redaction point and only while content capture is on.
Guarantees of an implementation: A sink never blocks the writer beyond its time limit, never throws into the loop, and never reads
Failure of an implementation: A slow, failing or dead sink is skipped for the event, its failure is recorded, and the outcome of
the run and the primary event file are unchanged.
Unknown-value rule: A sink ignores fields and event types it does not know. Event types that start with `x.` belong to
third parties; they are never projected and never change the read model.
Wave 1 implementations: The compatibility projection sink; the OTLP exporter; the Loki sink.
Content owner: 111 (core side, writer, conformance suite, sample sink). The compatibility projection sink: 144.
The OTLP exporter and the Loki sink: 128.
Proving test: Sink conformance: a slow sink, a throwing sink and a dead collector leave the outcome and the
